question: Should ClawHub create a reviewed-community trust tier, and if so what evidence, reviewer authority, revocation rules, and user-facing claims distinguish it from Official and automated scan or provenance signals?
rationale: Current main provides admin-controlled Official status and separate automated artifact evidence but no public review contract; defining a new badge changes the marketplace trust boundary and cannot safely be inferred from code alone.

options.title: Specify a vetted-community tier
options.body: Define package or publisher scope, evidence requirements, authorized reviewers, renewal and revocation, appeals, and wording that avoids implying OpenClaw ownership.

options.title: Document an official-only policy
options.body: State that community packages cannot request a verified badge and should rely on source linkage, provenance, scans, and publisher metadata.

recommendation.title: Specify a vetted-community tier
recommendation.body: Define package or publisher scope, evidence requirements, authorized reviewers, renewal and revocation, appeals, and wording that avoids implying OpenClaw ownership.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest history-backed routing candidate for the current official-publisher, badge, management, and adjacent plugin-trust surfaces.
